newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woodside says Cossack oil back up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woodside says Cossack oil back up.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Monday that daily production of about 90,000 barrels of crude had resumed over the weekend at the Cossack-Pioneer offshore oil platform after being suspended last week due to a cyclone.
However, Woodside was monitoring progress of another cyclone that has formed off Western Australia and threatens to disrupt output again later this week, spokesman Graeme Atherton said.

Cyclone Rachel is expected to generate gales with gusts up 90 km an hour between the coastal communities of Broome and Wallal and could extend southwest to Port Hedland, the Bureau of Meteorology said.
There were no immediate plans to once again disconnect the platform from its mooring, Atherton said.
"We will wait and see if it stays near the coast or heads out to sea before making any decsions," he said.
"We're not expecting anything before Wednesday of Thursday," he said.
At 2200 GMT, cyclone Rachel was estimated to be 125 km west northwest of Broome and 390 km northeast of Port Hedland and moving southwest at 10 km an hour parallel to the coast, the bureau said.
The bureau has issued a warning for a category two cyclone for coastal areas between Broome and Port Hedland. A category two cyclone carries winds of between 125 and 169 km an hour.
The latest disconnection of the Cossack Pioneer platform, on December 31, occurred with a near-full cargo on board, which was being prepared for transfer to an offload tanker, Atherton said.
Woodside's other offshore operations potentially in the path of the cyclone, the Goodwyn and North Rankin stationary facilities, do not suspend operations during cyclones, he said.
"They're fixed platforms and they maintain production," he said.
The platforms rest on piling situated in waters about 130 metres deep, he said.
Rachel marks the fourth cyclone of the 1996/97 season, which runs from November to March.
"We've found the in the past that the most severe cyclones to hit our area have tended to be in March and April," the spokesman said.

The Cossack Pioneer, which pumps crude oil and gas from the Wanaea and Cossack fields on the North West Shelf of the Indian Ocean has been plagued by weather-related and technical problems since it was commissioned in November last year.
The Barrow oil field operated by West Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (WAPET) is located about 400 km west of Port Hedland and also potentially in the path of Rachel.

Equal partners in the North West Shelf are units of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron Corp, Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Woodside.
WAPET is a joint venture of Texaco Inc, Chevron and Royal Dutch/Shell Group, each with two-sevenths stakes, and Mobil Corp, with one-seventh.
